gadget_plan.mathematical_rationale: The one-in-three relation holds exactly when at least one of the three outputs is true and no two are true. The OR3 constraint enforces at least one. The three NAND2 constraints enforce that no pair is both true. Since the outputs are the only variables, the existential quantifier is over an empty set of auxiliaries, so the conjunction of these four constraints is equivalent to the source relation.

gadget_plan.mathematical_rationale: The constraints gamma(a,b,c,x) and gamma(a,b,c,y) require x=1 if a=b=c=0, require x=0 if two of a,b,c are true, and are unsatisfiable if all three are true. The constraint gamma(x,y,x,y) enforces x≠y. Thus, for the allowed output tuples, exactly one of a,b,c must be true: if zero true, x=y=1 fails x≠y; if two true, x=y=0 fails x≠y; if three true, the first constraints have no solution. If exactly one true, choose x=0,y=1 to satisfy all.

gadget_brief.spec_correct_definition: def Spec.Correct (spec : Spec Gamma relation variableCount) : Prop := forall tuple : BooleanTuple relation.arity, relation.Holds tuple iff exists assignment : Fin variableCount -> Bool, spec.formula.Satisfies assignment and forall index, assignment (spec.outputs index) = tuple index

gadget_plan.mathematical_rationale: The source NAE-3 relation is expressed using two auxiliary variables. For a mixed tuple, the two gamma constraints with the auxiliaries always hold, and the third constraint forces the auxiliaries to be unequal, which is always satisfiable. For a constant tuple, both gamma constraints require the auxiliaries to take the opposite constant, but then they become equal, violating the third gamma constraint, so no assignment exists.
